object.title: Serbanuta's conjecture on attainable M-ambiguity sequences
object.statement: Let $\Sigma$ be an ordered alphabet. For words $u,v\in\Sigma^*$ and a letter $a\in\Sigma$, a word is **$M$-unambiguous** if it is not $M$-equivalent to any distinct word, where $M$-equivalence means having the same Parikh matrix. **Serbanuta's conjecture.** If $uaav$ is $M$-unambiguous, then $uav$ is $M$-unambiguous. Equivalently, if $uav$ is $M$-ambiguous, then $uaav$ is also $M$-ambiguous. This conjecture concerns the possible patterns of $M$-ambiguity under insertion of a repeated letter and was proposed as an open problem by Serbanuta; its resolution is not specified in the supplied text.
object.source_name: Wen Chean Teh and Ghajendran Poovanandran, “M-Ambiguity Sequences for Parikh Matrices and Their Periodicity Revisited”, arXiv:1901.03937 (2019).
